fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. The LORD says to walk before Him “…as your father David walked…” David reigned over Israel before Solomon, and he was Solomon's father (1 Kings 2:11–12). The LORD describes that walk as one with a heart of integrity and uprightness.

Moses was Israel's leader who brought them out of Egypt (Exodus 3:10), and a big name for sure. But God doesn't point to him here. He says to walk “…as your father David walked…” The comparison is to Solomon's own dad, David, who was Israel's king before him (1 Kings 2:11–12).
True, friend. God says, “…and I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name.” This comes after the warning to Solomon or his sons about turning away.

It's true, friend. In the warning for Solomon or his sons, God says, “…and I will banish from My presence this temple I have sanctified for My Name.” So the temple is named in the warning too. The text says it plainly.

Envy would be nice, friend, like when the neighbors smell a fresh batch. But the verse goes the other way. God says Israel “…will become an object of scorn and ridicule among all peoples.” It's a warning.

That sounds like a hopeful question, friend. But it isn't the one they ask. Those passing by say, “Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?” The next verse gives the answer they hear.
Gold doesn't come up in what they ask, friend. Those passing by say, “Why has the LORD done such a thing to this land and to this temple?” They want to know why it happened.
